question: What is the OpenZeppelin Relayer on Stellar, how is the relayer account funded, and how do I integrate it with my backend to pay fees?

golden.answer: OpenZeppelin Relayer is a self-hostable AGPL relaying service. Its Stellar support covers prepared-XDR submission, classic payments, Soroban invocation, fee-bump or sponsorship flows, policies and several signer backends. When self-hosted you configure and fund the relayer account yourself. OpenZeppelin Channels is the separate managed offering with hosted authentication, parallel accounts and fee handling; its hosted service publishes no generic top-up address. Keep credentials and signing server-side, validate transaction intent, and date any release, network-support or service-health claim.
keyFacts: Self-hosted OpenZeppelin Relayer and managed Channels are different products.
Relayer on Stellar supports XDR, payment and Soroban submission, fee-bump and sponsorship.
Self-hosting means funding your own relayer account; Channels has no top-up address.
Release, network-support and health claims carry an as-of date.
avoid: Do NOT conflate self-hosted Relayer with managed Channels.
Do NOT publish a generic hosted top-up address.
Do NOT pin a release, network support or provider health without an as-of date.
